accepted.name: met_objects_core
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  object_id,
  object_number,
  SAFE_CAST(is_highlight AS BOOL) AS is_highlight,
  SAFE_CAST(is_public_domain AS BOOL) AS is_public_domain,
  department,
  object_name,
  title,
  culture,
  period,
  dynasty,
  reign,
  portfolio,
  artist_role,
  artist_prefix,
  artist_display_name,
  artist_display_bio,
  artist_suffix,
  artist_alpha_sort,
  artist_nationality,
  artist_begin_date,
  artist_end_date,
  object_date,
  object_begin_date,
  object_end_date,
  medium,
  dimensions,
  credit_line,
  geography_type,
  city,
  state,
  county,
  country,
  region,
  subregion,
  locale,
  locus,
  excavation,
  river,
  classification,
  rights_and_reproduction,
  link_resource,
  metadata_date,
  repository
FROM `bigquery-public-data.the_met.objects`
accepted.description: Normalized projection of the Met objects table with cleaned, consistently named columns useful for joins and aggregations. Use this as the canonical objects dimension when combining metadata, filtering by artist/department/country, or computing object-level aggregates. | Use for: List objects by artist/department/country; Aggregate counts of objects by medium, period, culture, or department; Filter objects with public domain or highlight flags; Join object metadata to images or vision annotations

accepted.name: met_images_flat
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  object_id,
  original_image_url,
  gcs_url,
  title AS image_title,
  public_caption,
  caption AS image_caption,
  SAFE_CAST(is_oasc AS BOOL) AS is_oasc
FROM `bigquery-public-data.the_met.images`
grain: one row per image record (object_id + url combination)
accepted.description: One-row-per-image projection exposing image URLs, captions and a preserved object_id for joins. Useful when enumerating images by object, joining to vision annotations, or counting images per object. | Use for: Retrieve all image URLs for a given object or artist; Count images per object or per department; Join images to vision API annotations by object_id

accepted.name: vision_labels_exploded
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  v.object_id,
  la.description AS label_description,
  la.score AS label_score,
  la.confidence AS label_confidence,
  la.locale AS label_locale,
  la.mid AS label_mid
FROM `bigquery-public-data.the_met.vision_api_data` v,
UNNEST(COALESCE(v.labelAnnotations, [])) AS la
grain: one row per object_id + vision label
accepted.description: Explodes labelAnnotations from vision_api_data into one row per label per object with scores and description. Useful for searches, aggregations of label frequencies, or joining label-level data to objects/images. | Use for: Find objects containing a given vision label or keyword; Aggregate most common labels across the collection; Filter objects where label score or confidence exceeds a threshold (threshold applied downstream)

accepted.name: vision_faces_exploded
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  v.object_id,
  idx_off AS face_index,
  fa.detectionConfidence AS detection_confidence,
  fa.rollAngle AS roll_angle,
  fa.panAngle AS pan_angle,
  fa.tiltAngle AS tilt_angle,
  fa.joyLikelihood AS joy_likelihood,
  fa.angerLikelihood AS anger_likelihood,
  fa.sorrowLikelihood AS sorrow_likelihood,
  fa.blurredLikelihood AS blurred_likelihood,
  fa.underExposedLikelihood AS underexposed_likelihood,
  fa.headwearLikelihood AS headwear_likelihood
FROM `bigquery-public-data.the_met.vision_api_data` v,
UNNEST(COALESCE(v.faceAnnotations, [])) AS fa WITH OFFSET AS idx_off
grain: one row per object_id + detected face (face index)
accepted.description: Explodes faceAnnotations into one row per detected face per object including numeric detectionConfidence and pose angles. Useful for face-counting, quality filtering, and analyzing face attributes per object. | Use for: Count faces detected per object or per artist; Find objects with faces above a detection confidence threshold; Analyze pose/angle distributions of detected faces

accepted.name: object_image_vision_join
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.object_id,
  o.object_number,
  o.title AS object_title,
  o.artist_display_name,
  o.department,
  o.medium,
  o.object_date,
  i.original_image_url,
  i.gcs_url,
  i.public_caption,
  i.caption AS image_caption,
  v.fullTextAnnotation,
  v.safeSearchAnnotation
FROM `bigquery-public-data.the_met.objects` o
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.the_met.images` i
ON o.object_id = i.object_id
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.the_met.vision_api_data` v
ON o.object_id = v.object_id
grain: one row per image record (object_id + image url)
accepted.description: Denormalized join combining object metadata, image records, and vision annotation summaries at the object-image level. Exposes one row per image (object_id + image url) with selected object metadata and top-level vision fields to support downstream filtering and aggregation. Use when you need combined context for display or analytics. | Use for: Show images with object metadata and vision text/safety signals; Count images per object and examine associated vision annotations; Filter objects/images by safeSearch or presence of OCR (fullTextAnnotation)

accepted.name: object_label_counts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  vl.object_id,
  COUNT(1) AS label_count,
  AVG(COALESCE(vl.label_score, 0.0)) AS avg_label_score,
  SUM(COALESCE(vl.label_score, 0.0)) AS sum_label_score
FROM (
  SELECT object_id, la.description AS label_description, la.score AS label_score
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.the_met.vision_api_data`, UNNEST(COALESCE(labelAnnotations, [])) AS la
) AS vl
GROUP BY vl.object_id
grain: one row per object_id (aggregated label measures)
accepted.description: Aggregates counts and average scores of vision labels per object. Produces one row per object with label_count and avg_label_score, useful for ranking or filtering objects by richness of label annotations. | Use for: Rank objects by number of labels or average label score; Filter objects with no labels (label_count = 0) or rich labels; Join to objects to inspect high-label objects

accepted.name: objects_image_count_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.object_id,
  COUNT(i.original_image_url) AS image_count,
  DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(i.original_image_url) DESC) AS image_count_rank
FROM `bigquery-public-data.the_met.objects` o
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.the_met.images` i
ON o.object_id = i.object_id
GROUP BY o.object_id
grain: one row per object_id (aggregated image count and rank)
accepted.description: Computes the number of images per object and assigns a dense rank by image count so downstream queries can select top-N objects by image richness by filtering on image_count_rank. Exposes image_count and image_count_rank. | Use for: Find objects with the most images (top-k by image count); Filter objects that have no images (image_count = 0); Analyze distribution of images per object
